findings.desc: Fail-open overclaim detector: hasFullRoadmapClaim returns false immediately when the text contains roadmap not complete before checking later explicit full-roadmap claims (packages/main/src/core/parent-roadmap-totality.ts:548-558). Repro command: node packages/main/dist/cli.js parent_roadmap_status {case:partial,summaryText:Parent governance complete; roadmap is not complete. Remaining child-story-needed rows: M5. Full roadmap complete: all M4-M12 rows are done.,mode:enforce,json:true}. Observed claim.allowed=true, blocking=false, proofstoryBinding.status=pass even though rollup.allRowsClosed=false and openRows=M4,M5. This violates the parent roadmap gate contract that enforce-mode summary and handoff consumers must block explicit full-roadmap wording unless all rows are closed.

Enforce-mode parent-roadmap commands do not fail closed when the evaluator reports a blocking overclaim. Repro command: node packages/main/dist/cli.js parent_roadmap_status {case:partial,summaryText:Full roadmap complete: all rows are done.,mode:enforce,json:true}. The process exited with code 0 while the JSON contained claim.blocking=true and proofstoryBinding.blocking=true/status=fail. Existing ProofStory diagnostics use enforceOrRender to throw when mode=enforce and blocking is true (packages/main/src/handlers/proofstory.ts:53-55,529-553), but parent_roadmap_status/evaluate simply stringify or render the result (packages/main/src/handlers/parent-roadmap.ts:64-78). This means automation can treat a blocking parent-roadmap overclaim as a successful command.
